facts.raw_span: a 3-month history of brown-yellowish vaginal discharge
fluctuating lower abdominal pain
fever
progressive abdominal enlargement over 15 years, worsening in the last 5 years
difficulty with defecation and voiding
a smooth, firm pelvic mass was palpated extending to two fingers below the umbilicus, with limited mobility
the cervix could not be visualized or sondaged
elevated Cancer Antigen 125 level of 115.6 g/dL
a 269 × 529 mm hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity
a separate 126 × 106 mm homogeneous solid mass in the left adnexa with a clear border
a 145 × 110 × 146 mm multilocular cystic mass with thick septa and enhancing solid components
no lymphadenopathy was noted

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of a large pelvic mass, elevated CA-125 level, and imaging findings of a multilocular cystic mass with thick septa and enhancing solid components are consistent with leiomyosarcoma.
The patient's symptoms of brown-yellowish vaginal discharge, fever, and pelvic mass, along with imaging findings of a hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity, suggest infected hematometra.
The patient's history of a smooth, firm pelvic mass and imaging findings of a homogeneous solid mass in the left adnexa are consistent with a uterine fibroid.
The patient's imaging findings of a separate solid mass in the left adnexa with a clear border suggest an ovarian fibroma.
The patient's symptoms of brown-yellowish vaginal discharge and fever, along with imaging findings of a pelvic mass, suggest pelvic inflammatory disease.
The patient's symptoms of progressive abdominal enlargement and difficulty with defecation and voiding are consistent with adenomyosis.
The patient's elevated CA-125 level and imaging findings of a hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity suggest endometrial cancer.
The patient's symptom of difficulty with defecation is consistent with diverticulitis.

rationales.F01: Brown-yellowish vaginal discharge suggests infection or malignancy, but is not specific enough to rule in or out any concept strongly.
rationales.F04: Progressive abdominal enlargement over 15 years suggests a slow-growing mass, which could be a uterine fibroid, ovarian fibroma, or leiomyosarcoma.
rationales.F06: A smooth, firm pelvic mass is suggestive of a uterine fibroid or ovarian fibroma.
rationales.F09: A hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity is suggestive of infected hematometra or a uterine fibroid.
rationales.F11: A multilocular cystic mass with thick septa and enhancing solid components is suggestive of a malignant tumor, such as leiomyosarcoma or endometrial cancer.
